Source evidence: Milvus consistencyLevel is an enum {Strong, Session, Bounded, Eventually}. The probe sent 'INVALID_ENUM' which should be rejected at the proxy validation layer. However, API returned code 0 (success), meaning enum validation is MISSING or BYPASSED. This is a REAL BUG - enum values are not being validated despite being defined in the source.

Source evidence: consistencyLevel is defined as an enum field. Empty string '' is not a valid enum value. The API should either reject this (missing validation) or apply a documented default. Response code 0 indicates it was accepted without validation. This is a REAL BUG - enum validation is missing or empty values are not being handled.

Source evidence: The API may be doing case-insensitive enum matching (common in Go validators). 'strong' (lowercase) maps to 'Strong' (enum value). Response code 0 indicates it was accepted. This is BY-DESIGN - case-insensitive matching is a valid design choice.

comparison_to_baselines.single_LLM_no_source: 6.7% (1/15) - single LLM judgment WITHOUT source grounding
comparison_to_baselines.single_LLM_with_extracted_source_dev_rev: 27/27 (100%) - single LLM WITH extracted source on reviewer-killed candidates

key_findings.critical_insight: HTTP 200 != API acceptance. Must check response codes (0=success, 1100/1802=validation errors, 404=not found). Initial 'API accepted' metric was misleading.
real_bugs: consistencyLevel enum validation missing - INVALID_ENUM accepted
consistencyLevel empty string accepted - should reject or default
key_findings.most_common_reclassification_reason: Dimension and required field validations work correctly via error codes 1100/1802 despite HTTP 200 responses

conclusions.single_LLM_with_source_vs_without: Source anchoring improved precision from 6.7% to 16.67% (2.5x improvement) by filtering out 10 false positives that were actually by-design validation working correctly.
conclusions.gap_to_testvdb_remains: TestVDB at 69.2% vs single-LLM-with-source at 16.7% suggests multi-agent debate provides significant benefit beyond source anchoring alone.
conclusions.dev_review_discrepancy: A1 showed 100% (27/27) on reviewer-killed candidates with source extraction, but this end-to-end experiment only achieved 16.7%. Difference: A1 judged pre-filtered candidates (reviewer already eliminated obvious FPs), while this experiment judged raw probe results including all validation noise.

methodology_notes.probe_execution: All probes returned HTTP 200. Response codes in body determined actual acceptance/rejection.
methodology_notes.source_anchored_judgment: Applied Milvus source knowledge (enum definitions, validation logic, error codes) to classify each probe result as TP (real bug) or FP (by-design).
